newsitem.title: USA: Green groups seek U.S. sanctions on South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Green groups seek U.S. sanctions on South Korea.

text.p: Wildlife and conservation groups Thursday urged the U.S. government to impose trade sanctions against South Korea for failing to stop illegal trading of bear parts.
In a petition filed under a U.S. law to protect endangered wildlife, the groups said South Koreans were violating international treaties against trading in bear parts.
Bear gall bladders and bile are used in traditional Asian medicines and their paws are prized as an edible delicacy.

"Due to the extensive consumer demand and inflated street prices for the bear parts, a lucrative illegal trade has flourished, destroying bear populations in South Korea and threatening a variety of bear species throughout Asia," said the Sierra Club Legal Defence Fund.
The fund filed the petition on behalf of several groups including Defenders of Wildlife and Humane Society International.

It was filed to the Interior Department after Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky and Representative John Porter of Illinois reintroduced bills to stop involvement in the black market for bear parts and fluids.
The U.S. government has raised concern about South Korea's role in wildlife trade over the last few years, but has not threatened trade sanctions.
Officials at the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Korean embassy were unavailable for comment.
